lines.en: It’s night again. Which means that-
Okay. Well, I guess we’re just getting right into things this time then.
: Hello?
Consider yourself lucky, though. Because I had this whole thing I was about to say about worms and it was going to take a really, really long time.
: Good evening, Sensei. You’re not busy at the moment, are you?
: Not at the moment. Why? Are you looking to get fingered in another alleyway?
: Not even slightly.
: I guess that rules out clitoral stimulation too then. What’s up?
: If you’re through with your perverted antics, I’d like to inform you about a bit of a...situation here at the church.
: What, at Yasu’s church? There’s always a situation there. It’s probably your fault for going.
: No, it’s her fault for making me come to this blasted, disgusting...cathedral of unrepentant confusion! Do you think I want to be here?!
: No. I think you want me to be there, though. So I’ll just drop what I’m doing and head over now because I’m so infatuated with you.
: Thank you. Flattery will get you nowhere, however.
: It got me into your panties.

: No, it did not. The blame there lies entirely in the hands of hormones and the fact that my type is apparently hulking older men. Flattery was just the bridge we took for me to encounter my acceptance of this.
: Got it. So which alley are we meeting in this time?
: Goodbye. I’ll be waiting outside of the church to give you a more complete briefing of the situation.
: You’ll be debriefing me once the “situation” is over too then?
: If you’re good, we’ll see. But I wouldn’t get my hopes up because you have never been good a day in your life.
: Fair enough. See you, Touka. And probably Yasu as well since it would be weird for you to be there without her.
: Just hurry up and get here, okay?
So, back to that thing I was saying about worms-
Ahh...you don’t care. So, on second thought, let’s talk about God instead.
My mother was a believer. And I, at one point, am sure I believed in her.
But somewhere between “goodnight” and “moon,” a poison apple fell into my lap and taught me that the sweetest things in life are those determined to kill you.
Ever since then, I have been a masochist — just not the type to harden at the sight of whips or chains.
I’m the kind who speaks before he’s spoken to and only stays quiet at funerals. The kind who gains a feather in one of his wings each time someone passes down their pity or tells me to clean my room.
There’s a clock on the wall that stares at me sometimes. It has eyes once the little hand passes the twelve.
And each time it glances down, I glance back up. I ask it why the ticks feel more like flight than anything else.
And the clock looks into my eyes and says something like this.
: About time you got here. I’ve been waiting for nearly two hours.
: I had to bury something on the way My bad, darling. I am here now to make all of your troubles go away.
: Which would be wonderful if I were the one troubled at all. Also, please never call me “darling” again. It’s fine when my mother does it. But with you, the sarcasm is palpable and unsettling.
: So, what’s the deal? Give me this “briefing” you mentioned on the phone.
: Before that, may I ask you something? When was the last time you saw Ami?
: Ami? This morning. Why?
: And did she seem normal to you?
: I can not remember the last time Ami seemed normal to me in any capacity.
: Well,  yes. There is a certain baseline level of insanity we all attribute to her now. But I mean more along the lines of, has she been acting normal “for her?”
: I...guess? But why? What does Ami have to do with the church? Why is that important right now?
: Well, it’s important because Yasu has locked herself inside of the same prison she intended to make us fornicate in and will not stop rambling about her.
: What?...
: It’s been that way for several days, actually. And when the two cross paths at school, Yasu nearly breaks down in tears.
: Yasu breaks down in tears practically every five minutes and it’s always seemingly at random. That doesn’t mean anything.
: While that may be true, this seems...different.
: And, as the leading expert on Yasu and her mannerisms, I believe you have no choice but to trust my word on this.
: So either Ami did something to her...said something to her...or, equally as probable, Yasu dreamt something up and has now scared herself half to death because of it.
: All three of these seem equally likely to me, to be honest.
: I mean...Ami does “mess” with people. But she’d have no reason to do something like that to Yasu. In fact, I don’t think I’ve ever even heard her talk about Yasu before.
: What’s Yasu saying exactly? Has she told you why she’s acting that way?
: Of course she has. But that doesn’t mean I understand any of it. But perhaps you might since the two of you clearly have some sort of...connection. As difficult as that is for me to say.
: Alright then. Take me to jail. Let’s do this.
: You’re awfully comfortable saying those words. Have you been practicing them for when your world comes crashing down?
: Recited them in my head repeatedly that time I was making you cum in public.
: Oh, wonderful. Then you’ll be adequately prepared when I call the police the next time you bring that up.
Touka struggles to get the doors of the cathedral open, so I lend her a hand and we’re accepted right away.
Mannequins of all shape, size, and color line the stone pews — heads turning as we walk past them in search of the stairs but Touka doesn’t seem to notice.

I can hear them whisper. But, being conscious enough to know that this is all just in my head, I angle my chin down and contort the puppet strings that control my eyes in an effort to tangle them with Touka’s.
She moves with such elegance. Such grace.
It feels like she’s floating.
I feel like I’m floating.
: Aaaaand here we are. Good luck. I have aspirin in my bag if you need any.
: As well as all of Yasu’s medication. Which she has once again stopped taking and surely played absolutely no part in her current psychotic break. Isn’t that right, Yasu?
: I’m out of time...I’m out of time...
: Uhh...Yasu? Is there anything I can help with? Something Touka can’t, maybe?
: Bed me. Claim me. Pull my legs apart and pierce my body with the stake you keep between your legs.
: Oh, right. I also should have mentioned that she’s been rambling about this as well. I’ve likely just gotten so used to everyone else doing it that I forgot.
: Hold me down by my shoulders and fill me with your salvation. It is the only way to save me now.
: Yasu...did Ami say something to you? Was she here?
: I am a failure. A worm. And blind just like Him.
: My job is to see and I have failed even that. Yet she has seen it all. Things I can’t even describe. Things that even you have not seen.
: There are more shepherds than sheep in this slaughterhouse. And what does that make me?
: Bed me. Claim me. Fuck me. I will sin. I am sin. Just spare me and I will live out the rest of my days wading through a sea of atonement for chasing this nightmarish dream.
: We are so close and so far all at once. So many left to rot. Feasts for maggots who too will be feasted upon by the few left standing once He comes to claim us all.
: Fuck me. Fuck me. Fuck me. I need the light.

: Yes, so this is what I’ve been dealing with. She won’t come out. She won’t take her medication. She just lies there lamenting about the end of days, your niece, and the uncharacteristic desire to be bred.
: She is my daughter, Touka. Please stop calling her my niece. Please.
: Apologies, but her specific familial role matters very little to me right now when her mere existence has shocked my roommate to her very core.
: Yasu, did Ami do something to you? Can you come out of there and talk to us, please?
: No...This is where I must stay.
: This is the altar I must be sacrificed upon lest this vessel never earn its shield and everything we know is swallowed whole again.
: Yasu-
: I will die either way. But if I die here, at least I will die closer to the arms of God.
: There is no death, though. Just another plane, right? You’ve said it yourself a hundred times now.
: Far more than that. It’s a hundred just this month for me.
: I was wrong...
: Death is real...and it comes for us. Just like it came for her. Time....and time..and time...and time...and time...again.
: So much pain. So much torment. So many boxes. I can feel the rope tugging again. But it’s in so many directions now. And each way I look, something new has its tendrils wrapped around it.

: I am lost within the crowd. So if I wait here, I can be found. And He will tell me I am loved. That this wasn’t all for nothing. That We are the righteous and everyone else is a name engraved into the left leg of the torii.
: Or, alternatively, you can get out of that blasted prison cell and I can have someone on staff make you as many ichigo daifuku as you like. That sounds nice, doesn’t it?
: You shouldn’t be here, Touka...
: You shouldn’t see me like this...
: Take one of the other altars. Wormwood will show you the way. Then Sensei can save you too. And we can all face the flood together...
: But even then...it’s only two of each animal. And one of us will have to be tossed overboard.
: This isn’t what the angels told me. This isn’t what I’ve seen. But if all of that was not an illusion...then what?
: Come...
: Take it...
: Take this body and make it yours.
: Yasu, please-
: Take this flesh and eat it. Take this blood and drink it. Build a home between my fragile legs and christen it with the fruits of your unconscious gift.
: But even more than that...
: Please...make me forget what I saw.
: For this is a message I can not deliver. There is simply no time.
: So, what now? Do you have any experience picking locks? Or should we really just call the police and let them handle this instead?
: Yeah, definitely not the police.
: I mean, I’d obviously give you ample time to separate yourself from the situation first. She’s been in here all evening as-is. A few more hours wouldn’t hurt her.
: Is there a key somewhere? Maybe we could just-
: It’s in there with her. You think I haven’t tried that already?
: Okay. New plan, then. Go home, Touka.
: Go home?! And what? Leave her alone? Are we trying to starve her out now? Because there’s not a doubt in my mind her stubbornness will kill her sooner than she caves to hunger.
: No. Go home and let me handle this. You’ve done enough already.
: You wouldn’t.
: Touka-
: Akira, if you are even thinking what I assume you’re thinking right now, you are out of your fucking mind. I won’t allow it.
: That’s why I’m trying to separate you from the situation. You don’t want to-
: To have my friend lose her virginity in a basement during a psychotic episode?! You’re damn right, I don’t!  Yasu’s not fit to lose such a thing even normally and this is how you want to do it?!
: You’ll jump at any excuse to sleep with someone, won’t you?! And to top it all off, now I look like an idiot for thinking you’d be above taking advantage of this poor girl right now!
: You’re right. You are an idiot, Touka. You called a wolf to come check on a caged rabbit and now you’re surprised he’s hungry? That is on you.
: Wow.
: So that’s really how it’s going to be then?
: You’re going to do this your way and let me live with the guilt of what happens next?
: That’s right.
: Then why should I leave at all and not just foil your little “plan” by remaining here and starving myself beside her?
: Because you’re smart.
: I beg your pardon? Is that some sort of threat?
: It could be. Or there could be a method to this madness that your maternal instinct is pulling you away from right now.
: Maternal instinct. Again with this nonsense. These instincts are far from maternal. This is common sense, if anything.
: Yeah, well, you’ve always had more of that than me.
: You’re a pig.
: I’ll get her out of here. I promise. But it’s not something you’re going to want to be around for.
: If you lay a single finger on her-
: Touka...I’ve got this. And if you don’t trust me right now, trust yourself for trusting me in the first place.
: This is exactly the problem with wolves. They always look cute, but they can rip you limb from limb before you know it.
: You think I’m going to rip Yasu limb from limb?
: You’re hungry, aren’t you? There’s a rabbit right there. You said it. So what animal am I, I wonder?
: You’re not. You’re the sun in the background of the scene, slowly descending and letting nature run its course. Then the moon — rising up and keeping watch.
: And you’re a pretentious piece of shit who speaks like a romantic despite being the complete antithesis of one.
: Touka-
: I will have your head if harm befalls her. And the only reason I am biting your little hook right now is because the act of taking that head would bring me great joy.
: You’ll be a better mom than even yours one day.
: Then here’s hoping my children will grow up better than you.
I had a feeling that’s how Touka was going to react. What I didn’t know, however, was if she was actually going to leave or not.
I’m glad she did, though. Because I know she’s just trying to help, but she’s not ever going to think any of Yasu’s ramblings are actually legitimate.
And I know that I joke about them sometimes too, but...I do know that she knows some things.
And if any of those things involve Ami or something else to help me start putting this puzzle together, I need to know them.
Touka can hate me for it if she wants. But it’s what needs to be done.
: Thanks for letting me in. I like what you’ve done with the place.
: They’re all scared as well. We’re taking shelter from the end of days together.
: I see.
: Are you going to have sex with me now?
: Yasu, do you actually want me to have sex with you? Or are you only asking for this because you’re afraid of something you saw?
: “Afraid” does not begin to describe it. I need you to penetrate me if I’m to ever leave this cell. I can not face the outside world a second longer knowing I’m without armor.
: And what’s on the outside, Yasu? What happened with Ami that put you in such a...precarious position?
: She came here...
: Ami did? Why? I didn’t know about that.
: To learn.
: She spoke of her mother. Of things she both heard and saw when her time was running out.
: And then I touched her...
: Hands can be so strange...can’t they?
: How much they can hold. How little of it can be seen by most.
: For those of us that do see, though...
: It’s often far...far...far too much.
: You sure you want to listen to any of this, Aki-kun? Wouldn’t it be, like, way more fun to tear her panties off and deliver her from evil or whatever?
: Yasu...Ami’s mother didn’t appear to you, did she? An older woman who looks just like her?
: Aww, come on! You haunt three girls and suddenly none of them can be weird without it being your fault anymore?
: I’ve never even opened a door around this one. And I do that just to fuck with people sometimes.
: No...I’ve never seen anyone like that before. This was...this was Ami. Ami and...and something else...
: Something else as in what? What else did you see?
: E...Everything...
: It wasn’t just one something. It was so many of them! Each more perplexing than the rest! And the deeper it went, the darker they were!
: I could feel them inside of me. Fighting for me. It was so loud...and nothing I did could stop it! Even He could not lend me His hand for His hands held only slightly more than hers!
: Or is it Hers?...
: I...I don’t know anymore...
: And you...got all of this from just touching Ami’s hand?
: She’s lying. Ami’s not involved in any of this. I died before the curse could reach her.
: What curse?! What are you even-
